## Summary

- `misc/Info.plist` had an empty `<string/>` for `CFBundleShortVersionString`
- macOS uses this key to track app identity across updates; when it is empty the bundle version is treated as unknown, and macOS may silently drop `.qet`/`.elmt`/`.titleblock` file-type associations after a Gatekeeper re-evaluation or app update
- Set it to `0.100.1` to match the current `CMakeLists.txt` project version

## Context

Flagged in the #218 discussion as a follow-up to 8d7635464 (QFileOpenEvent routing fix). scorpio810 noted it in that commit message as "not included here."

## Notes

Ideally `CFBundleShortVersionString` would be populated dynamically via `cmake configure_file` so it tracks the CMake `VERSION` field automatically and never falls out of sync. That's a slightly larger change; this one-liner is a safe stop-gap that fixes the immediate problem.

## Test plan

- [ ] Build macOS bundle and confirm `CFBundleShortVersionString` is `0.100.1` in the resulting `Info.plist` inside the `.app`
- [ ] Double-click a `.qet` file after update — file association should be retained

An empty CFBundleShortVersionString causes macOS to treat each launch as
a version-unknown app, which can silently drop file-type associations
(.qet/.elmt/.titleblock) after an update or Gatekeeper re-evaluation.
Set it to the current project version (0.100.1) so the bundle is
correctly identified across updates.

Follow-up to #218 / commit 8d7635464 which fixed QFileOpenEvent routing.
